key_insight: The paper shows how to compute intrinsic Fréchet means on an unknown embedded Riemannian manifold using only local sampling and an observed distance metric, via a graph-based iterative approximation of geodesic interpolation.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical way to estimate nonlinear averages when data live on complex geometric spaces, such as manifolds of probability distributions or other non-Euclidean data representations.
method: Build a graph from adaptively sampled points on the unknown manifold.
Approximate geodesic interpolation using the graph and the observation metric only.
Run an iterative Fréchet-mean optimization with provable convergence guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an O(1/T) expected objective gap bound and numerical experiments showing effective intrinsic averaging with a sample complexity of ~O(T^{4d+3}) points.
watch_item: The sample complexity grows very quickly with intrinsic dimension, so the method may become expensive for higher-dimensional manifolds or limited sampling budgets.
paper_title: Computing Fréchet on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
